svg.title: Arbiter AI: one event, from evidence to explained decision
svg.desc: Collection and L1 rules lead to Qwen3.5:4b. Only Qwen escalations enter separate L2 guardrails and a pre-filter. Gemma4:12b receives original facts without Qwen opinion text when model judgment is useful. Shared final guardrails protect both stages and shortcuts. Known risk or missing context retains review; supported ordinary activity can be quieted. Both models are replaceable compatible local models. Classification grants no device-action rights.
svg.text: From raw evidence to a clear next step
Qwen is L1. Only its escalations go to Gemma L2 for a final review.
Gather reports without letting the AI change a device.
Read logs and alerts from the sources you enable.
Keep originals so a person can check what happened.
Put computer, user, time and network details in one format.
Reject broken records; keep the original evidence.
Save events in a waiting line
Save waiting events so a restart does not lose the queue.
Limit the queue; show when incoming work exceeds capacity.
Review urgent events first; let older waiting events progress too.
Link nearby events; check the computer's role and history.
Use approved facts only when they fit this exact event.
Safety rules check for known risky signals
Clearly routine, clearly risky, or still unclear?
Review unclear alerts and explain a recommendation.
This local model can be replaced by a compatible one.
Check the answer against rules and required evidence.
If the AI fails or is too unsure, ask a person to review.
Quiet the alert with a written reason.
Keep the record for later checks.
Show why it needs someone's attention.
A warning alone does not block anything.
Record the decision, evidence, and rule or model used.
Keep a history so a person can check the reasoning.
Show a person the next step
Explain what happened, where, and what needs checking.
Keep alerts visible while the second brain investigates.
Protect risky evidence; use exact human feedback.
Skip repeat reviews when needed context is missing.
Read original facts without Qwen's opinion text.
Propose a decision, then challenge it in another pass.
Known risk can veto quieting, whichever stage proposed it.
Keep the original decisions, reasons and deciding layer.
Keep the reason and both reviews.
WHO CAN AUTHORIZE A DEVICE CHANGE?
Alert decisions do not authorize commands, blocks or other actions.
Either model can be replaced by a compatible local model. Both reviews remain auditable.
Only Qwen escalations enter L2. Rules can avoid an unnecessary Gemma call.
